sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 (R180), WebGPURenderer, Rapier 2D compat 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, AI Hub Session 1.4.0; JavaScript and HTML/CSS
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded geometry, dark ink outlines, warm industrial storybook palette
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClips for workers and pests, with procedural secondary motion and particles
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated swing/chiptune music, synthesised effects and gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world host-authoritative co-op for 1–2; standalone couch co-op and same-origin tab rooms via BroadcastChannel
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripted physics, full campaign, native WebGPU, browser UI, emulated standard controllers, multitouch, audio synthesis and AI Hub harness checks; visual QA screenshots. Physical controller and real iOS behavior: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No internet research; native model knowledge. Supplied AI Hub integration files fetched as the implementation contract. Package dependencies downloaded.

testingFeedback: Testing and integration review caught 11 issues: progression resets, coin timing, four session/network edge cases, slider navigation, touch UI retention, fast taps, menu audio gating and result music scheduling.

5 could interrupt controller or multiplayer play: dedicated-server seat mapping, replacement-partner reconnection, hub navigation resetting a round, disabling a surviving seat, and waiting for blocked audio before menu actions. All were fixed.
The scripted full campaign with real Rapier physics, checking every phase, 23 pest kicks, 18 bonus coins and three boss hits.
Native headless WebGPU screenshots were blank on this software adapter; state checks and a WebGL backend visual capture were more useful.
engineFeedback: Three.js AnimationMixer, TSL materials and WebGPURenderer made procedural characters and ink shading straightforward.
Headless WebGPU rendered state correctly but did not yield a useful screenshot on this adapter.
The entire arcade ruleset, controller-first interface, procedural art/audio and host-authoritative session layer.
Keeping rigid-body head bumps and platform routes predictable while separating render animation from gameplay state.
Make software WebGPU headless image capture reliable and expose clearer backend diagnostics.
promptFeedback: The explicit source, controller-first goals and complete vertical-slice requirement gave a clear gameplay target.
No research was allowed while a network integration URL was required; I treated that URL as an implementation contract, not research.
Delivering art, five varied shifts, procedural audio, controller/touch controls and synchronized co-op in one HTML file.
Clarify whether standalone remote networking needs signaling infrastructure or whether AI Hub remote play plus local co-op is sufficient.

aiHub.name: Grit Bros
aiHub.description: Clock into a cel-shaded underground arcade: bump pests from below, boot them into brass, and beat the Big Clog. Five shifts, one bonus scramble, and drop-in two-player co-op.
aiHub.controls: Move: A/D or stick; jump/bump: Space or Cross/A; emergency thump: E or Square/X; auto-kick flipped pests; pause: Esc/Options. P2: J/L, I, O or second pad. Touch: drag left, hold right to hop.
